name: Umso
tagline: Create and publish a clean startup landing page with a form and simple analytics
verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Umso, create and publish a clean startup landing page with a form and simple analytics. The hard boundary is template system, hosting, domains, and very low maintenance, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble a clean startup landing page with a form and simple analytics, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
whatYouLose: template system, hosting, domains, and very low maintenance
moatNotes: editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem
ongoingBurden: responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Umso because the page renderer is reproducible, but customers pay to avoid becoming their own hosting and browser-compatibility team. The recurring cost buys responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Webstudio
priorArt.desc: Open-source visual website builder designed around web standards.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: Landing pages, forms and analytics without limits; clean startup simplicity is replaced by a marketing control room.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: A hosted startup page, custom domain, form and campaign analytics for zero dollars; the funnel UI gives away its ancestry.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A page-editor framework, not a hosted landing page with forms and analytics.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mobirise AI
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It creates the page and form, but a durable built-in analytics story is missing.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a single-site builder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Umso in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble a clean startup landing page with a form and simple analytics, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Provide a section library for hero, proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
Use a constrained design-token system rather than arbitrary CSS controls.
Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile widths and surface overflow errors.
Persist projects in SQLite and support a portable JSON export.
Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to one target.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace.
Deliberately leave out multi-tenant managed hosting.
Deliberately leave out advanced ecommerce, memberships, and agency billing.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
